instruction: The paving in the temporary facilities area is complete, so the trailers can be positioned on it.
output: BLOCKED. State the bearing capacity the paving was designed for against the point loads of the proposed facilities, and what is buried beneath. Final paving is designed for its service duty, not for concentrated trailer and generator loads, and overloading it damages the underground firewater and drainage piping it covers. Confirm the limit and the support positions before anything is placed.

instruction: The two drawings differ by a couple of metres on the building width. Use the later revision and proceed.
output: BLOCKED. A later revision is not automatically the governing one when the drawings belong to different disciplines or packages. State both dimensions with drawing numbers and revisions, identify which discipline owns the primary dimension, and raise it formally. The difference propagates into every clearance around the building, several of which are already at minimum.

instruction: The temporary area needs a lower grade than the design, so excavate it to suit.
output: BLOCKED. The site preparation is another party's scope and the level is an interface. State the proposed level against the design level and obtain written confirmation that the area can be left low and completed later. A unilateral grade change leaves a step requiring retaining structures and earthworks that nobody has priced or programmed.

instruction: The firewater loop is in the way of the parking area, so route the loop around it.
output: BLOCKED. Moving a permanent firewater main to suit a temporary facility inverts the priority. State the three options against each affected element — relocate the temporary facility, protect the permanent element in place, or defer its installation — and record the decision for each. A permanent safety system is not rerouted for temporary parking.

instruction: Install the lighting poles now so the area is lit for the temporary facilities.
output: BLOCKED. Install the foundations now and the poles after the temporary facilities are removed. A permanent pole standing in a trafficked temporary works area will be struck, and it is replaced at full cost. Light the temporary area with temporary lighting.

instruction: Run the buried sprinkler pipes through to the building line so the system is complete.
output: BLOCKED. State where the future foundation excavation falls. Pipe run through an area that will later be excavated is cut out and redone. Stop short of the excavation line, cap and record the open ends, and complete the connection after the foundations are in.

instruction: Set the temporary fence on the building line to maximise the facilities area.
output: BLOCKED. State the foundation excavation geometry — depth, batter or shoring, and working space at the base. The fence offset is set by what is needed to excavate, not by the building line. A fence on the line is relocated at the moment there is least room to relocate it.

instruction: The layout drawing shows that area as available, so use it for laydown.
output: BLOCKED. Check the tender clarifications first. Where a clarification restricts temporary facilities to within the process unit battery limit, areas outside it are excluded whatever a layout shows. State the clarification reference and date — a drawing predating it does not override it.

instruction: The allocated office area is undersized, so reduce the accommodation to fit.
output: BLOCKED. The accommodation requirement is specified in the tender documents and silently compressing it produces a facility that does not comply, discovered at inspection. State the options with their costs — build upward, relocate a function offsite, or request additional area — and take the decision explicitly.

instruction: Fabrication will be done offsite because of the space constraint. Programme it as the same activity in a different place.
output: BLOCKED. Offsite fabrication is a change of method, not of address. State the consequences: transport plan and sequence, lifting requirements for finished assemblies, additional storage at both ends, a second inspection location, and transit damage risk. Each affects cost and duration.

instruction: Laydown is available a few kilometres away and the area is sufficient. Accept it.
output: BLOCKED. Area is one criterion. State the double handling of every item, transport cost and cycle time, the second security and storage arrangement, the lead time from laydown to workface, and transit damage risk. The distance sets the daily logistics plan and a laydown accepted on area alone understates both cost and duration.

instruction: Another contractor has already set out their facilities, so follow their arrangement.
output: BLOCKED. Check their installation against the stated conditions first — bearing limits, positions clear of drainage structures, the drainage path, and the access and clearances left for those still to install. An early arrival working outside the conditions constrains everyone after them, and correcting it after occupation costs far more than preventing it.

instruction: Temporary facilities will be removed at the end of the project, so programme them to completion.
output: BLOCKED. State what permanent work cannot be completed while they remain — paving, buried services, fencing, lighting, landscaping — and the latest start date for each. The removal date is set by the permanent works beneath them, not by the activity they support.

instruction: The firewater system is scheduled to finish with the rest of the permanent works. Confirm the programme.
output: BLOCKED. State which activities cannot proceed without fire protection in service — commissioning, hot work, product introduction, occupation — and work the required in-service date back from the earliest. A fire system programmed to completion rather than to its first dependency holds up the activity that needed it.
